label: input 0 or u late in the original phase
explanation: Fires only during the original-input phase (never at t=0, the delimiter, or the copy phase). About 84% of activation mass is on steps whose input is the digit 0 or the letter u, with a weaker tail on d and f (and traces of q, h, 2). Firing becomes more likely later in the sequence: the rate rises with orig_idx (0.5% at t=1 to about 5% at t>=6) and with L, and is highest when few tokens remain before <DEL>. Even on 0/u it fires on only about 1/3 of eligible steps. Precision goes up (to about 0.55-0.69) when earlier inputs include 0/u/d or the previous token is from a similar set (u, d, 0, h, b, 2), so the unit seems to also depend on accumulated hidden-state context that I could not fully capture. The predicate t>=3 & input in {0,u} gets dev F1 0.47 and mass recall 0.79; adding d and f raises recall to about 0.82 but lowers precision. Top activations sit on 0/u near the end of the original sequence, often after other u/0/d tokens.
